clue.text: Media distribution officer gets money for each item afloat, it's reported?

indicators.note: something reported is spoken, so the phrase is said aloud and spelt by its sound

parts.note: money for each is PAY PER, and an item afloat is a BUOY

explanation.surface: A newspaper official earns a fee for every floating object, or so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: PAY PER BUOY said aloud gives the two words of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A humorous job title for the youngster who delivers newspapers on a round.

clue.text: Highway environmental hygienist, one howling on a Greek island, did you say?

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another comes after it
the question invites us to hear the island's name spoken and spell what we hear

parts.note: Rhodes is a Greek island in the Dodecanese
someone howling or crying is a weeper

explanation.surface: A street cleaner sobbing on a Greek island, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: A mock-grand title for a council worker who sweeps streets clean.

clue.text: Fail to break record that's exclusive

indicators.note: the failing word breaks into the record, splitting its two letters

parts.note: CD, a compact disc, is a record
to lose is to fail

explanation.surface: An athlete who fails to break a record that was exclusive.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed club or meeting is exclusive, open only to members.

clue.text: See 2
Australian native came across the empty sleeping car in America

parts.note: a roo, short for kangaroo, is native to Australia
met means came across

indicators.note: the word the is emptied of its middle, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A kangaroo encountered a vacant railway sleeper in the States.
explanation.definitionFit: In US railway usage a small private sleeping compartment is so called.

clue.text: Stuffing reindeer, I demonstrate less love, as gastronomical hygiene helper

indicators.note: the following pieces stuff the reindeer, sitting inside its name

parts.note: Dasher is one of Santa's reindeer

indicators.note: less means the zero for love is taken away from the word for demonstrate

parts.note: to show is to demonstrate
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A Christmas cook stuffing a reindeer, showing little affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuffing' looks like the cook's filling but signals a container; 'less' takes the tennis zero away, leaving SHW to join I inside Santa's reindeer.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand title for a kitchen appliance or person that cleans dishes after meals.

clue.text: Work, blah blah blah, less abundant for sanitation consultant

parts.note: to toil is to work
etc, et cetera, stands in for blah blah blah at the end of a list
leaner means more meagre, less abundant

explanation.surface: A consultant drones on about work and scarcity.
explanation.definitionFit: A mock-grand title for a bathroom cleaning product or the person using it.

clue.text: Long nail securing unsigned church regulations

indicators.note: the long nail holds the other piece fast inside itself

parts.note: a claw is a long nail
an unsigned work is anon, anonymous

explanation.surface: A long nail fixing a notice of church rules to a door.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of law governing a church, especially the Catholic Church.

clue.text: Prayer shawl initially bagged by hunter

indicators.note: the hunter bags the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: Orion is the hunter of Greek myth and the constellation

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of shawl

explanation.surface: A prayer shawl captured by a hunter.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic and literary word for a prayer.

clue.text: See 24
Huge creature in pram, wheels buckling

indicators.note: wheels buckling are bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A giant something sits in a pram whose wheels are buckling under its weight.
explanation.definitionFit: The cachalot is among the largest toothed animals on Earth, so huge creature fits.

clue.text: Papers in a sack, remained

indicators.note: the papers go in the phrase meaning a sack

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed
ID, identity papers

explanation.surface: Documents stuffed in a sack stayed there.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide is to stay or continue, so the past form is a synonym of stayed.

clue.text: Private school ultimately feeding parent, though not one daughter, as education centre nourishment technician

indicators.note: the following pieces feed into the parent, sitting inside it
only one of the parent's two daughter letters is dropped

parts.note: daddy is a parent
inner means private, as in inner thoughts

indicators.note: ultimately takes the last letter of school

explanation.surface: A private school pupil is fed by a parent, a convoluted job title for a canteen worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'though not one' matters: the parent has two D's and only one goes, leaving DADY, which 'feeding' fills after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mock-grand title for the woman who serves school lunches in Britain.

clue.text: Scatter around about ten cuttings

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about the Roman ten
the letters of scatter are thrown around into a new order

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Scatter cuttings around ten places in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Extracts are passages cut from a larger text, as press cuttings are.

clue.text: Flexible performer gave voice about my flips and tumbles, primarily

indicators.note: the whole combination flips over, read backwards
the word for gave voice goes about my

parts.note: sang means gave voice

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letter of tumbles

explanation.surface: An acrobat performs flips and tumbles while singing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flips' turns the whole container result (SANMYG) into GYMNAS; 'tumbles' looks like part of the act but only gives its initial.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete in gymnastics must be supple, hence a flexible performer.

clue.text: Condition of livestock causes amazement

definitions.meaning: a disease of sheep and horses causing staggering

explanation.surface: A farmer is amazed by an animal ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a livestock disease of lurching gait and a verb meaning astonishes.

clue.text: Extra soft back, hard in the middle, possibly?

indicators.note: the letter for hard is placed in the middle of the reversed letters
back says the combined words are read backwards

parts.note: spare means extra
P, piano, means soft in music
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A soft toy with an extra-firm centre, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: SPARE and P reversed give PERAPS; H goes in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Perhaps is a direct synonym of possibly.

clue.text: Colleague in amateur team finally welcomed by head

indicators.note: the head welcomes the pieces into itself

parts.note: pate is an old word for head
lay means amateur, non-professional

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of team

explanation.surface: A colleague in an amateur side is welcomed by the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A playmate is a companion in play, loosely a fellow or colleague.

clue.text: See 7
Wretched party game

parts.note: base means low, wretched
a ball is a dancing party

explanation.surface: A miserable party game.
explanation.definitionFit: A bat-and-ball sport, the US national pastime.

clue.text: Retreat a mockery — that's about right

indicators.note: the mockery goes about the letter for right

parts.note: a sham is a mockery

explanation.surface: Calling a retreat a mockery is about right.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious retreat or hermitage in India, a place for spiritual retreat.

clue.text: Block housing administrative subdivision for beverage dissemination officer

indicators.note: the block houses the subdivision inside itself

parts.note: to ban is to block
an arm is a branch or subdivision of an organisation

explanation.surface: A block housing an office that distributes drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A mock-grand title for the man who serves drinks in a pub.

clue.text: Male embraced by senior citizen who loves men and women, as recycling operative

parts.note: bi, short for bisexual

indicators.note: the grandmother embraces the letter for male

parts.note: a nan is a grandmother, a senior citizen

explanation.surface: A man hugged by a bisexual pensioner who sorts recycling.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a refuse collector, who takes away rubbish and recycling.

clue.text: Description of some bread, how else, in large fragments

indicators.note: the words broken into fragments are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: How else would you describe bread broken into big pieces?
explanation.walkthrough: 'else' is a link joining the two pieces of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread made with the whole grain kernel is described this way on the label.

clue.text: Bound to need clue, one of a pair for a start?

definitions.text: one of a pair for a start?

parts.note: to bound is to jump
a lead is a clue in an investigation

explanation.surface: A detective bound to need a clue to begin the case.
explanation.walkthrough: Jump leads come in pairs and start a car with a flat battery.
explanation.definitionFit: Booster cables come as two, used to start a vehicle with a dead battery.

clue.text: European agreement in ancient Hindu follower

parts.note: ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: A European nod of assent within an old Indian faith.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent of Jainism, an ancient Indian religion that grew out of Hindu tradition.

clue.text: Flier placed in mailbag — and erroneously

indicators.note: the bird is placed inside the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: A letter put in the wrong mailbag by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A male goose, a bird and thus something that flies.

clue.text: Make thin mice eat a soup

indicators.note: a soup is a jumbled mixture, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Starving mice are reduced to eating a thin soup.
explanation.definitionFit: To emaciate is to waste away the body, causing great leanness.
